item.question: Read the statement 'I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home.' Why is it a statistical statement, and what data is behind it?
steps: The rider has cycled home on many days.
Each day took a slightly different time, for example 13, 16, 15 or 14 minutes.
The word about tells us the times vary.
The number 15 sums up all those days in one value.
A claim that sums up data in a number is a statistical statement.
item.answer: It is a statistical statement because 15 minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day

item.question: In the second series Shubman scored 23, 7, 10, 52 and 18 in 5 matches. Yashasvi scored 26, 53, 2 and 15 and did not play one match. Who performed better on average?
steps: Shubman's total: 23 + 7 + 10 + 52 + 18 = 110 runs in 5 matches.
Yashasvi's total: 26 + 53 + 2 + 15 = 96 runs in 4 matches.
The totals come from different numbers of matches, so they do not compare fairly.
Shubman's mean: 110 ÷ 5 = 22 runs per match.
Yashasvi's mean: 96 ÷ 4 = 24 runs per match.
24 is more than 22, so Yashasvi performed better on average.

item.question: The first group's 33 estimates run from 42 to 68 seconds, with mean ≈ 58.21 and median 60. The second group's 28 estimates run from 47 to 71 seconds, with mean ≈ 59.29 and median 59.5. Which group fared better?
steps: First group: range 68 − 42 = 26 seconds; 20 of the 33 estimates are from 55 to 65 seconds.
Second group: range 71 − 47 = 24 seconds; 19 of the 28 estimates are from 55 to 65 seconds.
Both means are a little below 60, so on average both groups opened their eyes a little early.
The first group's median is exactly 60, but a few very early estimates (42, 45, 46) pull its mean down.
The second group's mean, 59.29, is closer to 60, and a larger share of its estimates (19 of 28) are within 5 seconds.
item.answer: Both groups did well; the second group was slightly better, with mean ≈ 59.29 closer to 60 and a smaller range of 24 seconds
